source.author: Gareth A. Jones
source.title: Primitive permutation groups containing a cycle
source.statement: Theorem 1.2 k=0: if a finite primitive degree-n group G not containing A_n contains a cycle with zero fixed points, then (a) C_p<=G<=AGL_1(p), n=p prime; or (b) PGL_d(q)<=G<=PΓL_d(q), n=(q^d-1)/(q-1), d>=2, q a prime power; or (c) G=L_2(11), M_11 or M_23 in degree 11,11 or 23 respectively.
source.scope: Public statement read from the specified version. The source explicitly says the proof relies heavily on finite-simple-group classification; its proof was NOT replayed or independently assessed.
